verses.1: 'My elder brother called Vali, capable of exterminating enemies was always highly regarded by my father and me.
verses.2: On the death of our father, the ministers, holding him the elder, installed this one as the highly esteemed king of the monkeys.
verses.3: 'I served him obediently like a servant while he ruled over the great ancestral kingdom inherited by him.
verses.4: 'Dundubhi's eldest son Mayabi was a mighty demon. He developed bitter enmity with Vali for the sake of a woman.
verses.5: 'One midnight when all were asleep, he (Mayabi) came to the entrance of Kishkinda screaming angrily and bellowing at Vali, challenging him to a duel.
verses.6: ' My brother Vali, who was asleep could not tolerate the frightful sound and jumped out of bed hastily.
verses.7: 'Enraged, he came out to kill the powerful demon even though I with the womenfolk (of the harem) tried to prevent him.
verses.8: 'That mighty warrior(Vali) came out, pushing aside all the womenfolk. I too followed him due to my affection towards him.
verses.9: 'On seeing my brother and me from a distance, the demon took to his heels scared.
verses.10: 'Frightened, he ran. We too chased him running faster. As the Moon was rising the path was welllit.
verses.11: 'The demon entered into a hole (cave) covered with a heap of grass, difficult, therefore, of access. Both of us reached there and took position.
verses.12: 'Seeing the enemy entering the cave, Vali became wrathful and his senses were terribly disturbed.He said to me:
verses.13: 'O Sugriva wait here at the entrance of the cave and be on your alert until I enter this hole and kill the enemy'.
verses.14: 'On hearing him, I begged the scorcher of enemies (Vali) that I would follow him, but he made me swear on his feet and entered the cave.
verses.15: Well over a year passed for him who had entered the cave, and that whole time passed for me as I waited at its entrance.
verses.16: 'Thinking him dead, I became agitated because of my love for him. My mind began to apprehend his death since I had not seen my brother for long.
verses.17: Then, after a long while, seeing frothy red blood flowing out of that cave, I became deeply grieved.
verses.18: 'I heard the roaring voices of the demons and not the yelling of my brother engaged in the duel.
verses.19: 'O friend by those signs I understood that my brother was killed and concluding that way I blocked the entrance of the cave with a rock of the size of a mountain and offered oblations to my brother and came to Kishkinda. I intended to hide the fact of Vali's death. But the ministers came to know the truth with their efforts.
verses.20: 'O friend by those signs I understood that my brother was killed and concluding that way I blocked the entrance of the cave with a rock of the size of a mountain and offered oblations to my brother and came to Kishkinda. I intended to hide the fact of Vali's death. But the ministers came to know the truth with their efforts.
verses.21: 'Then all the ministers assembled together and consecrated me. While I was ruling the kingdom lawfully, Vali, the monkey came back after killing the enemy demon.
verses.22: 'Seeing me on the throne, Vali became angry and his eyes turned red. He imprisoned my ministers and spoke to me harshly.
verses.23: 'O Rama even though I was capable of restraining the sinner, my intellect did not let me do so out of respect for my brother.
verses.24: 'When my brother came back to the town after killing the enemy, I offered as usual my salutations to him. But he did not bless me wholeheartedly.
verses.25: 'When my brother came back to the town after killing the enemy, I offered as usual my salutations to him. But he did not bless me wholeheartedly.
verses.26: 'O lord I bowed at his feet with my crown in total submission. Even then Vali was not pleased a bit. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे नवमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
